title: The risk register
grammar: Condicionais 1 e 2 (if + present → will / if + past → would)
objective: Nesta aula você vai falar de risco em inglês do jeito que o PMO exige. A primeira condicional trata do risco real e provável: 'If the pump is late, we will lose the milestone'. A segunda trata do cenário hipotético, usado para simular impacto sem assustar o cliente: 'If we lost the milestone, we would need a recovery plan'. A diferença entre as duas é política, não só gramatical.
intro: A risk register is a list of sentences that begin with if. If the supplier misses the delivery date. If the client changes the layout. If the rainy season starts early.

The tense you choose after if changes the message. If the pump is late, we will lose the milestone sounds like a real, live risk. If the pump were late, we would lose the milestone sounds like a simulation. Both are useful — on purpose.
vocab: If a new risk appears, we will add it to the risk register.
If we ordered a spare fan, the mitigation would cost fifteen thousand dollars.
If the contingency runs out, we will have to ask for a budget revision.
If the likelihood is high, the item goes to the top of the register.
If the impact were only financial, we could absorb it.
If the trigger occurs, the owner of the risk will inform the project manager.
practice: If a new risk appears, we will add it to the ______.
If we ordered a spare fan, the ______ would cost fifteen thousand dollars.
If the ______ runs out, we will have to ask for a budget revision.
If the ______ is high, the item goes to the top of the register.
If the ______ were only financial, we could absorb it.
If the ______ occurs, the owner of the risk will inform the project manager.
Every item in the ______ has an owner and a due date.
A good ______ plan is cheaper than the risk itself.

audio.title: Reviewing the top three risks
audio.text: Let me review the top three risks with you. First, the fan. If the supplier misses the July date, we will lose the erection milestone. That is a live risk, and the mitigation is a weekly expediting call. Second, the layout. If the client changes the layout after the design freeze, we will issue a variation order. Third, and this one is hypothetical, if we had to demobilise the civil crew for a month, we would lose about four hundred thousand reais and the whole sequence would move to the next quarter. I am not saying that will happen. I am saying that if it happened, that would be the cost.

readAloud: If the supplier misses the date, we will lose the milestone.
If the client changes the layout, we will issue a variation order.
If we lost the milestone, we would need a recovery plan.
If the contingency ran out, we would have to revise the budget.
If the trigger occurs, the risk owner will inform me.
fill: If the supplier ___ the date, we will lose the milestone. (miss)
If the client changes the layout, we ___ a variation order. (issue)
If we lost the milestone, we ___ a recovery plan. (need)
If the contingency ___ out, we would have to revise the budget. (run)
If the trigger ___ , the risk owner will inform me. (occur)
If we ___ a spare fan, the mitigation would cost fifteen thousand. (order)
If the impact ___ only financial, we could absorb it. (be)
We ___ the risk if the likelihood increases. (escalate)
qa: What happens if the fan is late?
If the fan is late, we will lose the erection milestone.
And if the client changes the layout?
If the client changes the layout, we will issue a variation order.
What would happen if you had to demobilise the crew?
If we had to demobilise, we would lose about four hundred thousand reais.
Is that a real risk?
No. It is hypothetical — but if it happened, that would be the cost.
What is the mitigation for the fan?
If we hold a weekly expediting call, we will see the delay much earlier.
sentences: If the supplier misses the date, we will lose the milestone.
If the client changes the layout, we will issue a variation order.
If we lost the milestone, we would need a recovery plan.
If the contingency ran out, we would have to revise the budget.
I am not saying it will happen — I am saying what would happen if it did.
If the trigger occurs, the risk owner will inform the project manager.
If the impact were only financial, we could absorb it.
Every risk in the register has an owner and a mitigation.
grammarPoint:
1ª condicional — risco real: If + presente → will + verbo.
If the pump is late, we will lose the milestone.

2ª condicional — cenário hipotético: If + passado → would + verbo.
If the pump were late, we would lose the milestone.

Regra que quase todo mundo erra: depois de if nunca entra will. O will fica só na outra metade da frase.
deepDive:
Por que a escolha é política: a 1ª condicional soa como aviso real ("isto vai acontecer se…"); a 2ª soa como simulação ("imagine que…"). Em reunião de risco com cliente, use a 1ª para o que está no registro como live e a 2ª para mostrar impacto sem criar alarme.

Variações da 1ª condicional: troque will por may / might / could (menos certeza) ou have to / must (obrigação): If the contingency runs out, we will have to revise the budget.

Na 2ª condicional, were serve para todas as pessoas em registro formal: If I were the client…, If the impact were only financial….

Sinônimos de if úteis em contrato: provided that (desde que), unless (a menos que), in the event that (na hipótese de). Unless the client approves it, we will not start. = If the client does not approve it…
examples: If the supplier misses the date, we will lose the milestone.
Se o fornecedor perder a data, vamos perder o marco.
If the client changes the layout, we will issue a variation order.
Se o cliente mudar o layout, vamos emitir um aditivo.
If we lost the milestone, we would need a recovery plan.
Se perdêssemos o marco, precisaríamos de um plano de recuperação.
If the contingency ran out, we would have to revise the budget.
Se a contingência acabasse, teríamos que revisar o orçamento.
Unless the client approves it, we will not start.
A menos que o cliente aprove, não vamos começar.
If the likelihood increases, we will escalate the risk.
Se a probabilidade aumentar, vamos escalar o risco.
If I were the client, I would ask the same question.
Se eu fosse o cliente, faria a mesma pergunta.
If the trigger occurs, the owner will inform the project manager.
Se o gatilho ocorrer, o responsável avisará o gerente do projeto.
mistakes: If the pump will be late, we will lose the milestone.
If the pump is late, we will lose the milestone.
Depois de if nunca entra will.
If we lost the milestone, we will need a recovery plan.
If we lost the milestone, we would need a recovery plan.
If + passado combina com would, não com will.
If the client would change the layout, we would issue an order.
If the client changed the layout, we would issue an order.
O would fica só na segunda metade da frase.
Unless the client doesn't approve, we won't start.
Unless the client approves, we won't start.
Unless já é negativo — não use outra negação.
If the impact was only financial, we could absorb it.
If the impact were only financial, we could absorb it.
Na 2ª condicional formal use were para todas as pessoas.
quick: If the fan ___ late, we will lose the milestone. (be)
If the client changes it, we ___ a variation order. (issue)
If we ___ the milestone, we would need a plan. (lose)
If the contingency ran out, we ___ the budget. (revise)
___ the client approves, we will not start.

celebrate.en: Excellent. A risk register is a list of if-sentences, and you now control both the real ones and the hypothetical ones.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Uma matriz de riscos é uma lista de frases com if — e agora você domina tanto as reais quanto as hipotéticas.

title: Variation orders and change requests
grammar: Linguagem diplomática — hedging (would / might / slightly / I'm afraid / seem to)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a dizer não ao cliente sem fechar a porta. Em inglês corporativo, 'This is not in the scope' soa agressivo; 'I'm afraid this would fall slightly outside the original scope' diz exatamente a mesma coisa e mantém a relação. Você vai montar essa camada de suavização com would, might, seem to, slightly e as fórmulas de abertura que os britânicos e americanos esperam ouvir.
intro: The hardest conversation in contract management is always the same one: explaining that what the client is asking for was never part of the deal. In Portuguese we soften it with tone of voice. In English you have to soften it with words.

The technique is called hedging. You keep the message exactly as firm as it was — the item is out of scope — but you wrap it in would, might, seem, slightly and I'm afraid. Nothing is lost. The relationship survives.
vocab: I'm afraid this would require a variation order.
Could we handle this through a formal change request?
This item seems to be slightly out of scope.
There would be a cost impact of around twenty thousand dollars.
The schedule impact might be as much as three weeks.
This requirement was not part of the original contract.
practice: I'm afraid this would require a ______.
Could we handle this through a formal ______?
This item seems to be slightly ______.
There would be a ______ of around twenty thousand dollars.
The ______ might be as much as three weeks.
This requirement was not part of the ______.
We are happy to do it, but it would need a ______.
Let me quantify the ______ before we decide.

audio.title: Explaining that an item is out of scope
audio.text: Thank you for the drawing. I have looked at it carefully and I would like to be transparent with you. The additional dust hood does seem to fall slightly outside the original scope of supply. The exclusion list in Annex two mentions all hoods downstream of the crusher, so I am afraid this one was not included. Having said that, we would certainly be happy to supply it. There would be a cost impact of around twenty thousand dollars and the schedule impact might be up to three weeks. Perhaps the simplest way forward would be a formal change request, so that everything stays documented for both sides.

readAloud: I'm afraid this would require a variation order.
This item seems to be slightly out of scope.
We would certainly be happy to supply it.
Perhaps the simplest way forward would be a change request.
There would be a cost impact of around twenty thousand dollars.
fill: I'm ___ this item is outside the original scope. (afraid)
This ___ to be slightly out of scope. (seem)
The schedule impact ___ be up to three weeks. (might)
Perhaps the simplest way forward ___ be a change request. (would)
We ___ certainly be happy to supply it. (would)
The cost impact is ___ twenty thousand dollars. (around)
This falls ___ outside what we agreed. (slightly)
qa: Is this hood included in your supply?
I'm afraid it seems to fall slightly outside the original scope.
Can you supply it anyway?
We would certainly be happy to supply it, with a variation order.
How much would it cost?
There would be a cost impact of around twenty thousand dollars.
Would it delay the project?
The schedule impact might be up to three weeks.
What do you suggest?
Perhaps the simplest way forward would be a formal change request.
sentences: I'm afraid this would require a variation order.
This item seems to be slightly out of scope.
We would certainly be happy to supply it.
Perhaps the simplest way forward would be a change request.
There would be a cost impact of around twenty thousand dollars.
Having said that, we are keen to find a solution.
This requirement was not part of the original contract.
Would it be possible to confirm that in writing?
grammarPoint:
Hedging = a mesma mensagem, com uma camada de proteção. Compare:

Direto: This is not in the scope. It will cost 20,000 and delay the project by 3 weeks.
Diplomático: I'm afraid this seems to fall slightly outside the scope. There would be a cost impact of around 20,000, and the schedule impact might be up to 3 weeks.

As quatro ferramentas:
1. Abertura — I'm afraid / Unfortunately / To be transparent
2. Modal — would, might, could no lugar de is e will
3. Verbo de distância — seem to, appear to, tend to
4. Atenuador — slightly, a little, around, somewhat, up to
deepDive:
Perguntas ficam mais educadas ao ficarem mais longas: Send me the drawing. → Could you send me the drawing? → Would it be possible to send me the drawing? → I was wondering whether you could send me the drawing.

A estrutura clássica de discordância: reconheça, depois discorde. I see your point, however, the exclusion list is quite clear on this. / Having said that, we are keen to find a solution.

Negativa suave em vez de negativa dura: That's wrong → That doesn't seem quite right. · I disagree → I'm not sure I'd agree with that. · We can't → That would be difficult for us.

Cuidado com o excesso: depois de suavizar, feche com um fato concreto (a cláusula, o anexo, o número). Diplomacia sem dado vira insegurança.
examples: I'm afraid this would require a variation order.
Infelizmente isso exigiria um aditivo contratual.
This item seems to be slightly out of scope.
Este item parece estar um pouco fora do escopo.
There would be a cost impact of around 20,000 dollars.
Haveria um impacto de custo de cerca de 20 mil dólares.
The schedule impact might be up to three weeks.
O impacto no prazo pode chegar a três semanas.
Would it be possible to confirm that in writing?
Seria possível confirmar isso por escrito?
I see your point; however, the exclusion list is clear.
Entendo seu ponto; contudo, a lista de exclusões é clara.
That would be difficult for us at this stage.
Isso seria difícil para nós neste estágio.
Having said that, we are keen to find a solution.
Dito isso, temos muito interesse em encontrar uma solução.
mistakes: I'm afraid that is not in the scope, you are wrong.
I'm afraid that seems to fall outside the scope.
Depois de suavizar não volte com uma acusação direta.
It would requires a variation order.
It would require a variation order.
Depois de would o verbo vem na forma base.
This item seem to be out of scope.
This item seems to be out of scope.
Sujeito singular pede seems.
Is possible to confirm in writing?
Would it be possible to confirm in writing?
Falta o sujeito it; e would deixa o pedido educado.
I am afraid for saying this is out of scope.
I'm afraid this is out of scope.
I'm afraid vem direto antes da frase, sem preposição.
quick: I'm ___ this is outside the scope.
This ___ to be slightly out of scope. (seem)
The impact ___ be up to three weeks. (might)
___ it be possible to confirm in writing?

celebrate.en: Very well done. You can now say no to a client in English and still be the person they want to work with on the next project.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você diz não ao cliente em inglês e continua sendo a pessoa com quem ele quer trabalhar no próximo projeto.

title: Reporting what the client and the supplier said
grammar: Discurso indireto + verbos de relato (agreed to, confirmed, warned, insisted on)
objective: Nesta aula você vai relatar reuniões com precisão jurídica. Numa disputa de escopo, quem registra melhor o que foi dito ganha a conversa. Você vai aprender o recuo dos tempos verbais ('He said the drawings were ready') e, principalmente, os verbos de relato que carregam intenção: confirmed, agreed to, refused to, warned, insisted on, denied.
intro: Minutes of meeting are not a transcript. They are a summary, written by you, that both sides will read six months later when the argument starts. Every verb you choose carries a legal weight.

He said he would check is neutral. He confirmed the delivery date is strong. He refused to accept the penalty is very strong. Today you learn the tense shift and, more importantly, the verbs that let you record exactly how firm a statement was.
vocab: The minutes of meeting confirm that the supplier agreed to the date.
The vendor confirmed that the fan would ship in September.
The client acknowledged that the change was requested by them.
We warned the client that the layout change would affect the schedule.
The client insisted on a witnessed performance test.
The supplier denied that the delay was their responsibility.
practice: The ______ confirm that the supplier agreed to the date.
The vendor did ______ that the fan would ship in September.
The client did ______ that the change was requested by them.
We had to ______ the client that the layout change would affect the schedule.
The client will ______ a witnessed performance test.
The supplier tried to ______ that the delay was their responsibility.
I need the vendor to ______ the date in writing.

audio.title: Reporting yesterday's meeting
audio.text: Let me summarise yesterday's meeting for the record. The client confirmed that the civil area would be released on the fifteenth of May. He acknowledged that the layout change had been requested by his own process team. We warned him that the change would affect the erection sequence and that a variation order would be necessary. He agreed to review the commercial proposal by Friday, but he insisted on a witnessed performance test before the final payment. The supplier denied that the delay was their responsibility and said that they had received the approved drawings only in March. I have recorded all of this in the minutes.

readAloud: He said the drawings were ready.
The client confirmed that the area would be released in May.
We warned him that the change would affect the schedule.
He agreed to review the proposal by Friday.
The supplier denied that the delay was their responsibility.
fill: The client confirmed that the area ___ released in May. (will be)
We warned him that the change ___ the schedule. (will affect)
He agreed ___ the proposal by Friday. (review)
The supplier denied ___ the drawings late. (receive)
She said she ___ the report the day before. (send)
The client insisted ___ a witnessed test. (on / have)
He told ___ that the budget was approved. (I)
qa: What did the client confirm?
He confirmed that the civil area would be released in May.
Did he accept responsibility for the change?
Yes, he acknowledged that his own team had requested it.
What did you warn him about?
We warned him that the change would affect the erection sequence.
What did the supplier say about the delay?
The supplier denied that the delay was their responsibility.
What did he insist on?
He insisted on a witnessed performance test before final payment.
sentences: He said the drawings were ready.
The client confirmed that the area would be released in May.
We warned him that the change would affect the schedule.
He agreed to review the proposal by Friday.
He insisted on a witnessed performance test.
The supplier denied that the delay was their responsibility.
He acknowledged that the change had been requested by his team.
All of this is recorded in the minutes of meeting.
grammarPoint:
No discurso indireto os tempos recuam um passo:
is → was · are → were · will → would · can → could · Past Simple → Past Perfect (had + particípio).

"The drawings are ready." → He said the drawings were ready.
"We will release the area." → He said they would release the area.
"I sent it yesterday." → He said he had sent it the day before.

say × tell: He said that… (sem pessoa) · He told me that… (sempre com pessoa).
deepDive:
Os verbos de relato são a parte que importa numa ata. Cada um tem sua estrutura fixa:

+ that — confirmed / acknowledged / denied / warned / explained / claimed that…
+ to + verbo — agreed / refused / promised / offered / threatened to do something
+ -ing — denied / suggested / admitted doing something
+ on + -ing — insisted on / apologised for doing something
+ pessoa + to — asked / told / advised / reminded someone to do something

Marcadores de tempo também recuam: yesterday → the day before · tomorrow → the following day · now → then · this week → that week.

Quando o fato ainda é verdade, o recuo é opcional: He said the fan has a twenty-week lead time continua correto, porque continua sendo verdade hoje.
examples: He said the drawings were ready.
Ele disse que os desenhos estavam prontos.
He confirmed that the area would be released in May.
Ele confirmou que a área seria liberada em maio.
We warned him that the change would affect the schedule.
Nós o alertamos de que a mudança afetaria o cronograma.
He agreed to review the proposal by Friday.
Ele concordou em revisar a proposta até sexta.
He refused to accept the penalty clause.
Ele se recusou a aceitar a cláusula de multa.
The supplier denied receiving the drawings late.
O fornecedor negou ter recebido os desenhos com atraso.
He insisted on a witnessed performance test.
Ele insistiu num teste de desempenho acompanhado.
He told me that the budget had been approved.
Ele me disse que o orçamento havia sido aprovado.
mistakes: He said me that the drawings were ready.
He told me that the drawings were ready.
Com pessoa use tell; say vai sem pessoa.
He confirmed that the area will be released.
He confirmed that the area would be released.
No relato, will vira would.
He agreed reviewing the proposal.
He agreed to review the proposal.
agree pede to + verbo.
He insisted to have a witnessed test.
He insisted on having a witnessed test.
insist pede on + verbo com -ing.
He denied to receive the drawings.
He denied receiving the drawings.
deny pede verbo com -ing.
quick: He confirmed the area ___ be released. (will)
He insisted ___ a witnessed test. (on / have)
He ___ me that the budget was approved.

celebrate.en: Outstanding. Your minutes of meeting now record not only what was said, but exactly how firmly it was said — and that is what protects a contract.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Sua ata agora registra não só o que foi dito, mas o quanto foi dito com firmeza — e é isso que protege um contrato.

title: The monthly report to the steering committee
grammar: Conectivos de causa, consequência e contraste (due to / as a result / whereas / despite)
objective: Nesta aula você vai transformar uma lista de fatos num relatório que se lê sozinho. A diferença entre um report amador e um executivo está nos conectivos: 'due to', 'as a result', 'therefore', 'however', 'despite', 'whereas'. Você vai aprender a estrutura de cada um — especialmente a armadilha 'because of + substantivo' × 'because + frase'.
intro: A steering committee has twelve minutes for your project. They do not want a list of events; they want a chain of cause and effect that they can follow without asking a single question.

The pumps arrived late. As a result, the erection slipped by two weeks. However, the civil works progressed ahead of plan, so the overall milestone is unchanged. Same facts, but now it is an argument instead of a list.
vocab: Due to the delay in erection, the earned value is below the plan.
Despite the change orders, the forecast at completion is stable.
Overall progress is 62 per cent, whereas the plan was 65 per cent.
As a result, we have prepared a recovery plan for the next quarter.
The variance is minus three per cent, which is within tolerance.
We increased the site headcount because of the recovery plan.
practice: Due to the delay in erection, the ______ is below the plan.
Despite the change orders, the ______ is stable.
______ is 62 per cent, whereas the plan was 65 per cent.
As a result, we have prepared a ______ for the next quarter.
The ______ is minus three per cent, which is within tolerance.
We increased the site ______ because of the recovery plan.
The schedule ______ is the number the committee looks at first.
A credible ______ needs dates, names and money.

audio.title: Two minutes at the steering committee
audio.text: Good afternoon. Overall progress is sixty two per cent, whereas the plan was sixty five. The variance is minus three per cent, which is within tolerance. This is mainly due to the late delivery of the pumps. As a result, mechanical erection slipped by two weeks. However, the civil works progressed ahead of plan, so the commissioning milestone is unchanged. Despite two change orders in the period, the forecast at completion is stable. We have therefore prepared a recovery plan, and we increased the site headcount by four people because of it. In short, the project is late in one discipline but healthy overall.

readAloud: Due to the late delivery, erection slipped by two weeks.
As a result, we prepared a recovery plan.
However, the civil works progressed ahead of plan.
Despite two change orders, the forecast is stable.
Progress is 62 per cent, whereas the plan was 65.
fill: ___ the late delivery, erection slipped by two weeks. (due to)
The pumps arrived late. ___ , erection slipped. (as a result)
___ two change orders, the forecast is stable. (despite)
Progress is 62 per cent, ___ the plan was 65. (whereas)
Erection slipped ___ the pumps arrived late. (because)
Erection slipped ___ the late delivery of the pumps. (because of)
The civil works were ahead of plan. ___ , the milestone is safe. (therefore)
___ the schedule pressure, the team kept the quality. (in spite of)
qa: Why did erection slip?
It slipped due to the late delivery of the pumps.
What did you do about it?
As a result, we prepared a recovery plan and increased the headcount.
Is the commissioning milestone at risk?
No. The civil works progressed ahead of plan, so the milestone is unchanged.
What about the cost?
Despite two change orders, the forecast at completion is stable.
How does progress compare with the plan?
Progress is 62 per cent, whereas the plan was 65.
sentences: Due to the late delivery, erection slipped by two weeks.
As a result, we prepared a recovery plan.
However, the civil works progressed ahead of plan.
Despite two change orders, the forecast at completion is stable.
Progress is 62 per cent, whereas the plan was 65.
The variance is within tolerance, therefore no action is required.
In short, the project is late in one discipline but healthy overall.
This is mainly because the pumps arrived four weeks late.
grammarPoint:
A armadilha número um do report:
because of / due to / owing to + SUBSTANTIVO → due to the late delivery
because / since / as + FRASE COMPLETA → because the pumps arrived late

Consequência (abre frase nova, com vírgula): As a result, / Therefore, / Consequently, erection slipped. Dentro da mesma frase, use so: The pumps were late, so erection slipped.

Contraste: However, (frase nova) · but (mesma frase) · whereas / while (compara dois dados) · despite / in spite of + substantivo · although / even though + frase.
deepDive:
Despite × Although — o erro clássico:
Despite the change orders, the forecast is stable. (+ substantivo)
Although we received two change orders, the forecast is stable. (+ frase)
Precisa de despite com frase? Acrescente the fact that: Despite the fact that we received two change orders…

Whereas serve para comparar, não para contradizer: Progress is 62 per cent, whereas the plan was 65. É a estrutura ideal para real × planejado.

Pontuação que o comitê espera: conectivo no início de frase leva vírgula (However, … / As a result, …). No meio, entre ponto-e-vírgula e vírgula: …is stable; however, the schedule slipped.

Fechamento executivo: In short, … / Overall, … / To summarise, … — uma frase, o veredito do mês.
examples: Due to the late delivery, erection slipped by two weeks.
Devido à entrega atrasada, a montagem atrasou duas semanas.
Erection slipped because the pumps arrived late.
A montagem atrasou porque as bombas chegaram atrasadas.
As a result, we prepared a recovery plan.
Como resultado, preparamos um plano de recuperação.
However, the civil works progressed ahead of plan.
Contudo, a obra civil avançou adiantada.
Despite two change orders, the forecast is stable.
Apesar de dois aditivos, a previsão está estável.
Although we received two change orders, the forecast is stable.
Embora tenhamos recebido dois aditivos, a previsão está estável.
Progress is 62 per cent, whereas the plan was 65.
O avanço é de 62%, enquanto o plano era 65%.
The variance is within tolerance; therefore, no action is required.
O desvio está dentro da tolerância; portanto, nenhuma ação é necessária.
mistakes: Due to the pumps arrived late, erection slipped.
Due to the late arrival of the pumps, erection slipped.
due to pede substantivo, não frase com verbo.
Because of the pumps were late, erection slipped.
Because the pumps were late, erection slipped.
Com frase completa use because, sem of.
Despite we received two change orders, the cost is stable.
Although we received two change orders, the cost is stable.
despite pede substantivo; com frase use although.
The pumps were late, however erection slipped.
The pumps were late; however, erection slipped.
however abre oração nova e leva vírgula.
Progress is 62 per cent, whereas is good.
Progress is 62 per cent, whereas the plan was 65.
whereas compara duas informações completas.
quick: ___ the late delivery, erection slipped. (due to)
Erection slipped ___ the pumps were late. (because)
___ two change orders, the cost is stable. (despite)
___ we received two change orders, the cost is stable. (although)
Progress is 62 per cent, ___ the plan was 65.

celebrate.en: Excellent. Your monthly report is no longer a list of events — it is an argument the committee can follow in two minutes.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Seu relatório mensal deixou de ser uma lista de acontecimentos: virou um raciocínio que o comitê acompanha em dois minutos.

title: Lessons learned and project close-out
grammar: Terceira condicional e should have (o que teria acontecido / o que devíamos ter feito)
objective: Nesta aula você vai fechar o projeto em inglês. Lessons learned exige uma gramática específica: a terceira condicional ('If we had frozen the layout earlier, we would not have lost three weeks') e o 'should have' ('We should have involved the electrical team sooner'). São as estruturas que analisam o passado sem acusar ninguém — e é assim que um close-out vira aprendizado em vez de briga.
intro: The close-out meeting is the only moment in a project when everyone is allowed to talk about what did not happen. It is also the meeting where English usually breaks down, because it needs the most complex structure in the language.

If we had frozen the layout in March, we would not have lost three weeks. We should have involved the electrical discipline earlier. Nothing can be changed now — and that is exactly what these two structures express.
vocab: If we had recorded the lessons learned earlier, the next project would have started better.
The close-out report should have been issued within thirty days.
We should have closed the punch list before the hand-over.
If the punch list had been closed, final acceptance would have come in June.
The retention would have been released earlier if the documents had been complete.
We should have updated the as-built drawings during erection, not after.

audio.title: The close-out meeting
audio.text: Thank you all for coming to the close out. Let me be honest about three lessons. First, the layout. If we had frozen the layout in March, we would not have lost three weeks in detailing. Second, the electrical discipline. We should have involved them in the kick off meeting, not two months later. Third, documentation. If the as built drawings had been updated during erection, final acceptance would have come in June instead of August, and the retention would have been released much earlier. None of this is anyone's fault. It is a list of things we will do differently on the next contract.

grammarPoint:
3ª condicional — o passado que não aconteceu:
If + had + particípio → would have + particípio.
If we had frozen the layout, we would not have lost three weeks.
(Não congelamos → perdemos as três semanas.)

should have + particípio — o certo que não fizemos:
We should have involved the electrical team earlier.
We shouldn't have started detailing before the freeze.

As duas falam de algo impossível de mudar. É por isso que aparecem justamente no close-out.
deepDive:
Contrações que você vai ouvir em call: If we'd frozen… (= had) e …we'd have lost (= would). O mesmo 'd vale para os dois; o que diferencia é o que vem depois.

Na passiva: The report should have been issued in thirty days. / The retention would have been released earlier. Muito comum em close-out, porque tira a pessoa da frase — e é justamente isso que evita a briga.

Primos úteis do should have:
could have done — era possível e não fizemos
might have done — talvez tivesse acontecido
needn't have done — fizemos, mas não precisava

Condicional mista — causa no passado, efeito no presente: If we had updated the as-builts, the client would be satisfied today.
examples: If we had frozen the layout, we would not have lost three weeks.
Se tivéssemos congelado o layout, não teríamos perdido três semanas.
We should have involved the electrical team earlier.
Deveríamos ter envolvido a equipe elétrica mais cedo.
We shouldn't have started detailing before the freeze.
Não deveríamos ter começado o detalhamento antes do congelamento.
The report should have been issued within thirty days.
O relatório deveria ter sido emitido em trinta dias.
If the punch list had been closed, acceptance would have come in June.
Se a lista de pendências tivesse sido fechada, o aceite teria vindo em junho.
We could have avoided the rework with one extra review.
Poderíamos ter evitado o retrabalho com mais uma revisão.
The retention would have been released earlier.
A retenção teria sido liberada mais cedo.
If we had updated the as-builts, the client would be satisfied today.
Se tivéssemos atualizado os as-builts, o cliente estaria satisfeito hoje.
mistakes: If we would have frozen the layout, we would not have lost time.
If we had frozen the layout, we would not have lost time.
Depois de if entra had + particípio, nunca would have.
If we had frozen the layout, we would not lost time.
If we had frozen the layout, we would not have lost time.
Falta o have: would + have + particípio.
We should involved the electrical team earlier.
We should have involved the electrical team earlier.
Para o passado é should have + particípio.
The report should have issued in thirty days.
The report should have been issued in thirty days.
Na passiva entra been: should have been issued.
We should have not started detailing.
We shouldn't have started detailing.
A negativa vem no modal: shouldn't have.
